newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UEFA AND ENGLAND CALL HALT TO WORLD CUP ROW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA AND ENGLAND CALL HALT TO WORLD CUP ROW.

text.p: UEFA and the English F.A. called a truce on Friday in their row over bidding for the 2006 World Cup finals.

Europe's governing body agreed that both England and Germany will make presentations of their bids in April. A final decision on which UEFa-backed country submits a bid to FIFA will be taken in December 1998.
UEFA and F.A. officials said after their three-hour meeting that they were keen to avoid damaging competition between England and Germany.
"UEFA is doing its upmost to have a harmonious bidding process within its federation,' said UEFA general secretary Gerhard Aigner. He said the april meeting would be held in Geneva.

The F.A. said they were delighted with the outcome. "In the end we hope there will be rules laid down in Geneva which will apply for World Cup bidding in the future," said F.A. general secretary Graham Kelly.
UEFA denied it had backed down but said the situation had changed since last week when it openly supported Germany's bid.
"UEFA had agreed to put forward one bid. Now we have two bids and we have to decide," Aigner said.
